bib.title: Searching for Best Practices in Retrieval-Augmented Generation

question: Which implementation choice for each module of the RAG workflow (classification, chunking, embedding, retrieval, reranking, repacking, summarization, generator fine-tuning) gives the best trade-off of performance and latency?
contributions: Through extensive experimentation, we thoroughly investigated existing RAG approaches and their combinations to identify and recommend optimal RAG practices.

We introduce a comprehensive framework of evaluation metrics and corresponding datasets to comprehensively assess the performance of retrieval-augmented generation models, covering general, specialized (or domain-specific), and RAG-related capabilities.

We demonstrate that the integration of multimodal retrieval techniques can substantially improve question-answering capabilities on visual inputs and speed up the generation of multimodal content through a strategy of "retrieval as generation".

method.summary: Three-step search: compare representative methods per RAG module on module-specific benchmarks, then test one method at a time per module in the full pipeline (others fixed at the best so far, going in workflow order), then propose two recipes. Final pipeline evaluated on five task families with a Llama2-7B-Chat generator fine-tuned with gold plus random context, over a Milvus index of 10M Wikipedia and 4M medical texts.

models.name: LLM-Embedder
models.architecture: embedding model (about three times smaller than bge-large-en)

models.name: zephyr-7b-alpha
models.architecture: generation model in chunk-size study; also query rewriting

models.name: Llama-2-7b
models.architecture: generator fine-tuned with LoRA and int8

other.note: Section 4 says Llama2-7B-Chat fine-tuned with random plus relevant documents is the generator; Appendix A.5 says Llama-2-7b base

training.objective: generator: negative log-likelihood of ground-truth output y given query x and context D

inference.temperature: 0.7 for HyDE hypothetical document generation (gpt-3.5-turbo-instruct); greedy otherwise
inference.max_tokens: 100 new tokens for open-domain and multihop QA; 50 for other datasets; HyDE up to 512 tokens
inference.samples: single run per configuration; 500 examples per dataset; no seeds or variance reported
inference.retrieval: typically 50 documents retrieved as input to the reranker; retrieved docs truncated to 2048 words for RankLLaMA and LongLLMLingua; summarization ratio 0.4; hybrid alpha 0.3; chunk overlap 20 tokens

parameters.sparse_dense: BM25 (Pyserini, Lucene) and Contriever; Faiss Flat index for dense
parameters.HyDE: 1 pseudo-document concatenated with query chosen over 8

metrics.name: Faithfulness / Relevancy (chunking)
metrics.definition: LlamaIndex evaluation module; faithfulness = response not hallucinated vs retrieved texts; relevancy = retrieved texts and response match query

metrics.name: mAP, nDCG@10, R@50, R@1k, latency
metrics.definition: TREC DL19/20; R@k order-unaware; latency per query

metrics.name: MRR@1, MRR@10, MRR@1k, Hit Rate@10
metrics.definition: MS MARCO dev rerank of BM25 top-1000; MRR@10 official

metrics.name: F1 and token count (summarization)
metrics.definition: F1 of generator answer and number of tokens after summarization

metrics.name: Ground-truth coverage
metrics.definition: used for generator fine-tuning because answers are short

metrics.name: Acc / EM / F1
metrics.definition: accuracy for commonsense, fact check, medical; token F1 and lenient EM (generation includes gold answer) for ODQA and multihop

metrics.name: RAG score
metrics.definition: average of Faithfulness, Context Relevancy, Answer Relevancy, Answer Correctness (RAGAs, GPT-4 judge) and Retrieval Similarity (cosine of retrieved vs gold document embeddings)

metrics.name: Avg. Score
metrics.definition: calculated from the Acc, EM and RAG scores for all tasks

baselines: no classification / no reranking / no summarization ablations
eval.protocol: Greedy sequential module search; each cell is a single run on up to 500 sampled examples; no significance tests, no seeds. Metrics from RAGAs with GPT-4 as judge.

prompts.text: [Instruction] Please generate ten descriptions for the continuation task. [Context] For example: 1. "French.Washington played a crucial role in the American Revolutionary War, leading the Continental Army against the British." Please continue writing the above paragraph. 2. "The discovery of the double helix structure of DNA by James Watson and Francis Crick ..."

limits: Authors concede they only fine-tune the generator, not the retriever or joint training.
Chunking was only tested for representative techniques due to the costs of building vector databases; metadata addition left to future work.
Modules are optimised greedily in workflow order, not over all combinations, so interactions are not explored.
Single run per configuration, 500 sampled examples per dataset, no variance or significance reported.
Chunk-size and chunking-technique studies use one document (lyft_2021 first 60 pages, about 170 generated queries) and a weak generator/judge setup.
Text numbers in Section 4.2 for query classification (0.428 to 0.443, 16.41 to 11.58 s) do not match the Table 11 classification rows.
Multimodal extension (Section 5.2) is described qualitatively with no measurements.
Latency is measured on unstated hardware; models are mid-2024 (Llama-2-7B, Llama3-8B, monoT5).

terms.definition: forward repacks documents by descending relevancy scores from reranking, reverse arranges them in ascending order, sides places relevant information at head or tail of the input
Small-sized blocks are used to match queries, and larger blocks that include the small ones along with contextual information are returned.
S_h = alpha * S_s + S_d, with normalized sparse and dense relevance scores
